summary: The cross-framework bridge: CNs, every, no, subtyped sentences (under explicit lifting) and the donkey sentence agree DEFINITIONALLY between CL20's MTT-semantics and Ranta 1995 (cumulativity does the sort bookkeeping); intersective adjectives are separated subsets (sig/sigT equivalence both ways); the strong donkey reading transfers through the shared currying theorem. The one genuine divergence is proof relevance: Ranta's Sigma projects witnesses as a function, MTT's Prop-existential returns them only up to inhabited — Coq's elimination restriction is exactly the formal residue of R95-Type vs CL20-Prop. Subtyping exists as a package only on the MTT side; sugaring only on the Ranta side.
